questions.text: What can you do with an object held by const?
options: Replace the object with another one. const allows that
Change its properties. const forbids assigning the name again, not writing into the object
Nothing. The object is frozen too
Only read properties. Writing a property throws TypeError

questions.text: What does a parameter do when it has the same name as an outer variable?
options: It hides the outer variable inside the function. The outer value does not change
It writes to that same outer variable
That name is forbidden. It is a SyntaxError
It is visible both inside the function and in the code that called it

questions.text: When can you already call the name of a function declaration?
options: Only after the line that declares it
Only if there is no var with the same name above it
From any line in that scope. The declaration puts the function in the name before the body runs

questions.text: What happens if you call a function expression stored in var above the assignment line?
options: It returns undefined, with no error
ReferenceError, as when reading let before initialization
TypeError. The name already exists, but it holds undefined until the assignment

questions.text: A function’s local var is not visible to the code that called it.
If an if block never runs, a var inside it is not created.
The same block can declare let twice with one name.
A new call of a function does not see the local var values left by the previous call.
Where is the name from catch (e) visible?
questions.answer: Only inside that catch. Outside the block the name does not exist.

questions.text: Can you write const without an initial value?
questions.answer: No. The initializer is required in the same declaration, or it is a SyntaxError.

questions.text: What does typeof return for a name that is not declared anywhere?
questions.answer: The string "undefined". That typeof does not throw ReferenceError.

questions.text: What does an assignment to an undeclared name do in strict mode?
questions.answer: It throws ReferenceError. No global property is created.
